items.title: Qualifying Madness in Les Gets with Asa Vermette and Gracey Hemstreet - The Setup | FOX
items.description:
After a few weeks away following Andorra, the circus rolls into Les Gets, where a passionate home crowd will be out in force to back the French riders.
 
But this weekend could be about more than home advantage. With a questionable forecast on the horizon, conditions could get rough, unpredictable, and seriously muddy. If the weather turns, expect sliding rear wheels, sketchy lines and plenty of surprises as riders battle their way down the track.
 
In this episode of The Set Up, we look ahead to what’s coming in Les Gets, the home crowd advantage, the French charge, and how the weather could shake up the form book for Round 7. Asa Vermette remains in the conversation for the overall, while Gracey Hemstreet won here last year in similar conditions. We’re excited to see how things unfold on race day and who’s done their homework over the summer break.
 
Welcome to Les Gets. Welcome to The Set Up.

items.title: The Fight | THE GRIND - Episode 2 | A Monster Energy Documentary Series
items.description:
Nine rounds. Three riders. One season.

The races keep coming, the fatigue is growing, and the pressure is always there.

Follow Luca Martin, Gwendalyn Gibson and Charlie Aldridge through the next chapter of the 2026 UCI Cross-Country World Cup season, as they take on Lenzerheide, La Thuile and Pal Arinsal.

At this stage of the season, the roles are beginning to take shape. Luca is fighting to defend the overall lead after an incredible run of results. Charlie is fighting his way back to his best after a difficult start to the season. Gwendalyn continues to deliver consistent results while facing the growing physical demands of the UCI World Cup circuit.

From intense battles on the course to crashes, recovery, team briefings and the moments between races, Episode 2 goes beyond the results to explore what it takes to keep pushing when the season starts to take its toll.

Three riders. Three different battles. One season that is only getting harder.

More than a race recap, The Grind explores the people behind the results, revealing the pressure, the fatigue, the setbacks, the rivalries and the reality of life on the UCI Cross-Country World Cup circuit.

The season is getting harder. The fight is just beginning.

Presented by Monster Energy. 🟢

items.title: The Fastest Man in Ireland (Ronan Dunne)
items.description:
Ronan Dunne races the clock on his home-built black track in Djouce Wood, Ireland. 
One target: under 55 seconds.

The double Red Bull Hardline winner grew up riding these woods in County Wicklow. Now he returns to the track he built himself, treating it like a personal time trial lab: full commitment through roots, rock gardens and blind hits, run after run, shaving tenths where most riders just survive.

items.title: "There Was Nothing Pro About Me" | Ronan Dunne on Just Ride
items.description:
Ronan Dunne joins Rob Warner and Eliot Jackson for one of the most honest conversations yet on Just Ride.

From missing qualifications and battling serious injuries to winning UCI Downhill World Cups and Red Bull Hardline, Ronan shares how his mindset has evolved, why he still embraces risk, and what it really takes to compete at the very top of downhill racing.

They also dive into training, recovery, Red Bull Hardline, growing up in Ireland, and the journey from being known as the "wild man" to becoming one of the fastest riders in the sport.

items.title: Why Kate Courtney Walked Away From the World Cup Grind | Just Ride
items.description:
Kate Courtney joins Rob Warner and Eliot Jackson for one of the most honest conversations we've had on Just Ride.

From becoming a World Champion at a young age to questioning whether she should retire, Kate opens up about rebuilding her career, creating She Sends Racing, recovering from injury, winning Leadville, becoming Marathon World Champion, and why taking risks has transformed the way she races.

It's a conversation about purpose, resilience, and finding success on your own terms.

items.description:
1199 delivered. 

On home soil, Jackson Goldstone put down a statement run to take the win at Crankworx Whistler, charging one of the most demanding tracks in the world.

And that was just a sample. In September, the world’s best downhill racers return to 1199 for the UCI Downhill World Cup — September 25–27, 2026.

The stage is set. See you back on 1199.
